themes.theme: Great businesses that are hard to buy
Seduced by big dividends in lousy industries

positions.commentary: Southwest Airlines came in and clobbered USA Airlines because they were low-cost providers.
The speaker bought Google at five and kept it because it was going rapidly.
Francis bought Apple at 160 bucks, which is a double digit P.E.

thesis: This episode argues that investors should avoid obvious great businesses like Google that are difficult to buy, while also warning against seduced by big dividends in lousy industries like airlines. It highlights the success of low-cost providers like Southwest Airlines that clobbered competitors, and notes that some investors bought Apple at a double-digit P.E. ratio.
